label: The sapu orchestrator: Step 0 scope-locks the run and holds the repo's sweep marker, so a second /sapu session stops there; Phase A drains every open PR; Phase B works each open issue as one Workflow call, several lanes in parallel, where a forge worker scouts read-only into a compact plan and a fresh builder of the same tier (one per slice when the plan is sliced) opens a PR in its own worktree, the qa specialist or a red Opus pair reviews it, and fix cycles (at most two; on red up to five, only while they converge) or a handoff past the worker's step budget follow; ready PRs go through a merge queue in sapu-merge.sh (gate, flake ledger, merge, mergeAfter); each session ends by rewriting the sapu-sweep-state memory page, plus a cleanup when the repo's policy says session; the last session runs the cleanup the policy sets, a final full gate and the final report, which also lists the engine defects filed on the plugin's repository. Workers never merge.
desc: Step 0 runs the scope lock (account, git email, origin, allowed roots, and a HOME that is the account's own), then holds the repo's sweep marker, so a second /sapu session on the same repo stops there, and reads the profile and policy. Phase A drains all open PRs: inventory, classify (READY, NEEDS-FIX, STALE, DRAFT, NEEDS-AI), review by risk tier, then merge through sapu-merge.sh; a PR closed as STALE, or blocked when its fix cycles run out (the same rule as a lane's), is not merged. Phase B triages open issues (SKIP, DUPLICATE, POLICY GAP, WORK) and runs each WORK issue as one Workflow call of sapu-wave.js, a lane: up to `lanes` in flight (1 to 4, computed from the machine), and a new lane starts as soon as one returns. In a lane a forge worker from the ladder first scouts the issue read-only and writes a compact plan, then a fresh builder of the same tier implements from that plan in its own worktree and opens a PR; a plan the scout slices gets one fresh builder per slice, and only the last opens the PR (fix cycles and escalated workers stay one phase); the qa specialist reviews every tier at Opus/high, and a red issue, a red-area diff, an unrun red-area check or the worker's own red-area report brings in an adversarial Opus pair (qa plus a domain specialist). Findings get fix cycles (a large round goes to one fixer per file group), each with a delta re-review: at most two on green and yellow; on red up to five, but past the second only while each review reports fewer findings than the one before and no finding is reported by three reviews in a row, otherwise the lane is blocked with the reason; a finding class (the rule a reviewer names) that comes back after its fix gets one structural redesign at Opus/high instead of another patch, and back again after that it goes to the owner; a judgment call escalates one step up the ladder once; a worker past its step budget (the contract's tuning) hands off to a fresh worker of the same tier while each handoff brings a new commit (two without one in a row block it, at most five per step). Ready PRs enter the merge queue: one sapu-merge.sh run at a time, in the background, awaited by notification; it runs the gate, records every run in the flake ledger, merges and calls mergeAfter. A red gate is never merged and is re-run at most once; red again, the failing files run on origin/base, where red means a base flake with one flake issue, fixed at its source. The end-of-wave net runs the full suite on the base branch at the cadence the profile sets. When a session reaches its context limit (a share of the model's context window, at most 350k tokens by default, from the contract's tuning), it rewrites the sapu-sweep-state memory page (one page, at most 40 lines, open items only), cleans up when the repo's policy.cleanup is session, and the owner starts a fresh session that resumes from that page. The last session, with no work and no open PR left, cleans up unless the policy is never, runs a final full gate and writes the final report, listing each engine defect filed on the plugin's repository. The policy is set once in /sapu:init. Cleanup runs sapu-cleanup.mjs, which prints its plan, then with --apply deletes only sapu's own branches proven merged and removes only their clean worktrees. The guard hook checks every subagent; the orchestrator only gets a reminder, one call in ten, once its context passes the contract's session limit; no subagent writes the plugins it runs under.
title: /sapu — the backlog orchestrator
